before: Runtime baseline: all 3 new tests fail. Both parsers and native software playback reject nine authored valid no-sample interval movies as unsupported MP4 track-fragment header flags. Plain finite control assertions complete before aggregate failure. Contradictory-run and overflow witnesses fail at the unrelated unsupported-flag check.
change: Support tfhd.duration-is-empty without manufacturing sample entries. Maintain a per-track decode cursor independent of sample-list tails, apply the explicitly present or inherited default duration, preserve tfdt overrides, and include a trailing empty interval in track duration. Refuse every trun in an empty-duration traf, even a zero-row run, and check its end timestamp.
after: 42 distinct integration checks pass across 10 targets, including expanded 4-test regression. Ten valid 3-picture controls include explicit V0/V1 and omitted tfdt, leading/middle/trailing gaps, inherited/zero duration and consecutive gaps. Both parser wrappers agree on packet bytes, DTS/PTS, nominal duration and track endpoint; software playback retains analytic YUV, RGB, exact intervals, 120 seek positions with continuation, rewind and repeated EOF. Exact three-sample budget passes and two-sample budget refuses, so gaps do not consume sample entries. Locked offline no-default-features core build check passes.
fixtures: 16 byte-identical regenerated files: 12 own short colored VP9 movies, 3 analytic YUV16 oracles and manifest. No private media/parameters, FFmpeg or network; ordinary tests use saved files only.
scope: One valid no-sample-fragment compatibility improvement, including its clock, byte-base and malformed/resource controls. No separate count for fixture variants or replacing sample-tail clock inference.
limitations: Playback retains its existing hold-until-next-picture interval behavior across middle gaps; no generated black-frame policy is introduced.
A trailing gap extends track duration without inventing or retiming the last picture.
An entirely sample-free track remains refused by the existing no-samples policy.
Dedicated playback is software; no GPU parity, performance or full project-wide green claim. Historical unrelated failures remain separate.
source_note: Only explanatory comments changed after the integration run; runtime code is unchanged.
